prompt: Let $\mathcal C$ be a class of finite simple graphs. For positive integers $d,m$, let $\mathrm{TM}_m(d)$ denote graphs with an $m$-colour tree-model of height $d$. All height and colour-count quantifiers below range over positive integers. Which statement defines bounded shrubdepth of $\mathcal C$?

answers.explanation: A single height and a single finite colour bound must work for the whole class. The actual tree and adjacency signature may vary.
Every finite graph has a height-one model using one colour per vertex. Per-graph bounds make the condition vacuous.
Choosing a different unbounded colour count for each graph again allows every graph at height one.
This demands models at every height, including height one, and is stronger than bounded shrubdepth.
The height must also be uniform. Unbounded-height one-colour models already include all cographs, whose shrubdepth is unbounded.
A model for one member gives no uniform control over the whole class.
The definition requires some sufficient bounds, not every possible choice of bounds.

answers.text: There exist positive integers $d,m$ and one fixed finite rooted tree $T$ that models every $G\in\mathcal C$, with height $d$ and at most $m$ leaf colours.
answers.explanation: Tree size must be allowed to grow with the number of graph vertices.

answers.text: $\exists d,m\;\forall G\in\mathcal C:$ the model has at most $m$ leaves and height $d$.
answers.explanation: The bound is on leaf colours, not on leaf count; the class may contain arbitrarily large graphs.

answers.text: $\exists d,m\;\forall G\in\mathcal C:$ the model has height $d$ and maximum branching $m$.
answers.explanation: Bounding height and branching bounds the total number of leaves. Bounded shrubdepth does not bound graph order.

sources.title: Ganian et al. — Shrub-depth: Capturing Height of Dense Graphs, §§2–4
